payload.headline: Micron falls 4.53% to 601.25; waiting for 471.0 or the December 17 report

summary.thesis: Micron is earning record profits, but its 74.59% operating margin is at a five-year peak, and today's price already assumes most of that peak lasts.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy only near the 471.0 support. Swing: no trade before the 2026-12-17 earnings report.
summary.act_at: Buy at 471.0; move to hold on a close above 659.6; trim above 833.11

payload.happening: MU fell 4.53% to 601.25. It sits below its falling 20-day (742.8) and 50-day (895.41) averages, so the trend is down. There is no new news since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2026-12-17, and options are pricing a 19.6% move through the 2026-12-18 expiry.
payload.business: The business itself is very strong right now. Over the last twelve months revenue rose to 133.2B from 37.4B. The latest quarter grew 345.03% from a year earlier, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) reached 59.0B, up from 1.7B. The balance sheet is not at risk: 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt leaves 40.6B of net cash. Dilution is low at 1.78% a year. The real question is margin. The operating margin jumped to 74.59% from 26.14%, and the filings note that it is at the top of a five-year range running from -41% to 75%, adding that peaks like this usually fade. Memory chips have historically gone through boom-and-bust pricing cycles (general knowledge), so what is at risk is how long these profits last, not whether the company survives. Today's drop and the downtrend reflect sentiment and the market's mood. Nothing in the data shows that demand or the company's competitive position has changed yet.

worth.text: A normal discounted-cash-flow model (a value built by projecting future cash) is not shown, because a one-year jump in free cash flow from 1.7B to 59.0B can't be projected forward. The other methods disagree. Against its own history, MU's price-to-sales range is 322.32 to 833.11, with a middle of 490.66, so the price is above the middle. Against peers it looks cheap: price-to-sales is 5.1 versus a peer median of 7.4, and the trailing P/E is 8.1. Working backwards, the 601.25 price implies free cash flow shrinking by about 4.6% at the start. If cash flow simply holds flat (0% growth), the value is 721.87. The gap between methods comes down to one thing: how long the peak margin lasts. The margin scenarios (1184.92 at a 55% margin, 801.92 at 37%) assume 20% starting growth, so they are optimistic. I put fair value between the own-history middle and the no-growth value.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow holds near 59.0B (0% growth) rather than shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin fades from the top of its five-year range.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 59.0B from 1.7B, and net cash is 40.6B, so the company can fund itself through a downturn.
It looks cheap against peers: price-to-sales of 5.1 versus a peer median of 7.4, and a trailing P/E of 8.1.
The price implies free cash flow shrinking 4.6% at the start; flat cash flow alone would justify 721.87.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin sits at the top of a five-year range that reached as low as -41%. Peaks like this usually fade.
The price is 601.25, below the falling 50-day average of 895.41, in a downtrend of lower highs and lower lows.
The put/call open-interest ratio is 2.16 (far more bets on a fall than on a rise), and options price a 19.6% move around the 2026-12-17 report.

levels.what: Top of the 435.76–471.0 support zone (a price floor that has held 5 times), close to the 490.66 own-history middle. Buy here.
Top of the 642.41–659.6 resistance zone (a price ceiling). A close above it would end the breakdown and move the call to hold.
Top of the own-history range. Trim above it, because that price assumes the peak margin lasts.

longterm.why: At 601.25 the price is inside the 490.66–721.87 fair-value range, so there is no margin of safety before the margin question is answered. The downtrend gives no reason to buy early.

swing.why: Resistance starts at 642.41, just above the price, which leaves little upside. The nearest support is 471.0, so a sensible stop would sit far away, and the average daily range is already 68.78.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-17 report can gap the price through any level. There is no new position until it shows whether the operating margin holds, unless the price reaches 471.0 first.

change_mind: A close above 659.6, the top of resistance, would move the long-term call from wait to hold.
If the 2026-12-17 report shows the operating margin holding near 74.59%, the case for the upper end of the range (721.87) gets stronger.
If the report shows the margin falling toward 37% and the price breaks below the 435.76 support, the call moves to avoid until the 351.92–369.12 zone.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait for 471.0. The 4.53% drop to 601.25 below the falling 50-day average of 895.41 confirmed that the downtrend gives no reason to buy early.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
